description:
Our website, which is an online Space Academy, provides users an experience through the visualization of past NASA mission data into an immersive journey. Our online interactive gallery of Artifacts will allow you to view retired spacecrafts such as Apollo lunar module, Spirit, Opportunity, and InSight, for you to learn about:

Identity & Function: Who the spacecraft is, what its function was, and the scientific devices it used.

• Location: Where is each of these artifacts currently placed.
summary:
Team ASTRA-X built ASTRA-X Space Academy, an interactive web app that turns NASA’s discarded equipment on the Moon and Mars into stories students can explore. It covers 24 real explorers, from the Surveyor landers and Apollo descent stages to Viking, Opportunity, InSight and Ingenuity. Each one appears on 3D globes of the Moon and Mars at its real landing coordinates and tells its own story in first person: why it went, what it discovered, how its mission ended, and where it rests today.

To meet the storytelling challenge, the app uses NASA photographs, official NASA 3D models and NASA landing-site terrain. It includes 20 real-time 3D mission videos with narration, an Earthrise scroll journey, AR views, and games based on real missions. Quizzes, badges and fun facts help students learn while they play. Every fact links back to a NASA source, and simulations are clearly labelled.

This matters because more than a hundred pieces of NASA hardware lie silent on other worlds, and most people have never heard of them. Our ASTRA-X turns these “abandoned” machines into heritage sites students can visit and learn science from. The app runs offline on laptops and phones.
details:
What it does and how it works

ASTRA-X Space Academy is an interactive web app that tells the stories of 24 NASA explorers that were left behind on the Moon, on Mars and in deep space. It runs entirely in the web browser, on a laptop, PC or phone, and works offline from a single HTML file.

  • 3D Moon and Mars maps: NASA imagery of the Moon and Mars wrapped onto globes, with each explorer marked at its real landing site. Tap a marker to open the explorer’s story, told in first person: why it went, what it discovered, its final days and where it rests today. Each story links to its NASA source.
  • 20 real-time 3D mission videos: one for each Moon and Mars explorer, plus “Twelve Moonwalkers”. They use NASA’s official 3D models and NASA’s 3D landing-site terrain, with automatic narration and captions.
  • Earthrise Journey: a cinematic scroll story that recreates Apollo 11’s flight from Earth to the Moon in 3D.
  • Solar System and Deep Space: live 3D views with planets at their approximate real positions for today’s date, and probes like Pioneer, Dawn and Kepler.
  • AR Mission Lab: places a NASA Moon or Mars globe over the camera view.
  • Games: Land the Eagle and Opportunity’s Last Drive, with 49 non-repeating NASA fun facts, plus the “Who Am I?” quiz.
  • Learning extras: a rule-based AI mentor answering from the app’s fact library, XP, ranks, badges, a certificate, a 3D photo vault of real NASA images and a sources page.

Benefits

  • Free and offline: no installation and no internet needed, so it suits classrooms with weak connections.
  • Hard-to-find knowledge in one place: history and science that is usually scattered across NASA archives.
  • Accessible: narration, captions, a reduce-motion setting, a light theme, adjustable text size, keyboard controls and a simple-language mode.
  • Trustworthy: facts are labelled “Verified”, “Simplified” or “Simulated”, and the 3D videos are marked as recreations.

Intended impact

Most people don’t know that more than a hundred pieces of NASA hardware sit silently on other worlds. ASTRA-X turns these “abandoned” machines into heritage sites that students can visit, care about and learn from. The aim is to spark interest in space science and engineering, and in protecting space heritage, especially among school students who may never visit a museum or NASA centre.

Tools, languages, hardware and software

  • Languages: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, and GLSL for the graphics-card shaders.
  • Graphics: WebGL, three.js (r147) with its glTF loader, the Draco 3D decoder, Canvas 2D and Google model-viewer for the AR Lab.
  • Browser features: Web Speech API for narration, getUserMedia for the AR camera, and local storage to save progress.
  • NASA data:
    • NASA Science 3D Resources: models of the Lunar Module, Astronaut, Viking, Opportunity, Ingenuity and InSight, plus landing-site terrains.
    • NASA SVS CGI Moon Kit: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter colour and elevation maps.
    • NASA Image and Video Library, JPL Photojournal, NSSDCA, and the NASA Planetary Fact Sheet.
  • Development help: built with help from Claude (Anthropic’s AI assistant). Disclose this if your submission rules ask about AI use.
  • Hardware: any laptop, PC or phone. A webcam or phone camera is only needed for AR.

What makes it creative

  • Machines tell their own stories: each explorer narrates in first person.
  • Real NASA 3D content, not cartoons: real NASA models and terrain bring each mission back to life in 3D.
  • Real details: dust follows lunar gravity, Earth appears where it really sits in each landing site’s sky, and Mars frost, ice polygons, dust storms and blue sunsets match each site.
  • Learning through play: games, fun facts, quizzes and badges keep students exploring.

Factors the team considered

  • Accuracy: every fact traced to a NASA source, with simplifications clearly labelled.
  • Age-appropriate design: kid-friendly fonts, colourful navigation and clear language.
  • Performance: detail adjusts automatically so it stays smooth on phones and older laptops.
  • Offline use: works without internet, for classrooms with limited connectivity.
  • Accessibility: the options listed under Benefits.
  • Privacy: no account, no server and no tracking. Progress and camera video stay on the device.
  • Copyright and ethics: only public-domain NASA material, credited with its NASA IDs. No real astronaut likenesses are created. Imagined future scenes are labelled.
